events.title: Justinian I publishes the second edition of the Codex Justinianus
events.description: Emperor Justinian I published the second edition of the Codex Justinianus, known as the Codex Repetitae Praelectionis, which superseded the first after his new laws had left it out of date. It took effect on 30 December.

events.title: Queen Margaret of Scotland dies
events.description: Margaret, wife of Malcolm III, died in Edinburgh Castle days after learning that her husband and eldest son had been killed at Alnwick. Celebrated for her piety and church reform, she was canonised in 1250.

events.title: Edward I becomes King of England on Henry III's death
events.description: On the death of King Henry III, Prince Edward, still travelling on the Ninth Crusade, became King of England as Edward I. He did not return to England for nearly two years.
events.html: On the death of King Henry III, Prince Edward, still travelling on the Ninth Crusade, became King of England as Edward I. He did not return to England for nearly two years.

events.title: An auto-da-fé at Ávila concludes the Holy Child of La Guardia case
events.description: An Inquisition auto-da-fé held outside Ávila ended with six conversos and two Jews burnt at the stake. They had been accused in the case of the Holy Child of La Guardia, a medieval blood libel.
events.html: An Inquisition auto-da-fé held outside Ávila ended with six conversos and two Jews burnt at the stake. They had been accused in the case of the Holy Child of La Guardia, a medieval blood libel.

events.title: Pizarro captures the Inca ruler Atahualpa at Cajamarca
events.description: Francisco Pizarro's force of fewer than 200 men ambushed Atahualpa's retinue in the square of Cajamarca, killing thousands. Holding the Inca ruler captive gave the Spanish leverage over a vast empire.

events.title: Gustavus Adolphus is killed at the Battle of Lützen
events.description: A Swedish army under King Gustavus Adolphus, supported by troops from Saxony and Hesse-Kassel, narrowly defeated an imperial force under Albrecht von Wallenstein at Lützen. Both sides suffered heavy casualties, and Gustavus himself was among the dead.

events.title: The British capture Fort Washington on Manhattan
events.description: British and Hessian troops stormed Fort Washington, the last American stronghold on Manhattan, and took about 2,800 prisoners. Washington's army retreated across New Jersey.

events.title: UNESCO's constitution is signed in London
events.description: Delegates of 37 countries signed the constitution of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It promotes cooperation in education, science and culture and lists World Heritage Sites.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto's party wins Pakistan's general election
events.description: The Pakistan Peoples Party, led by Benazir Bhutto, won the most seats in the first open election in over a decade. Weeks later she became the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority democracy.
